text:
customer_mark: Hey team — we've got multiple customers reporting partial SSE streams. They get a few chunks then the connection drops. Client shows code 200 but stops receiving events mid-response. Happens across our hosted API and on Dedicated in one cluster. Started after a config change last week.

support_john: Sorry to hear that — can you paste one example request/response and timestamps? Are clients reconnecting automatically?

customer_mark: Repro with curl attached:
```
curl -v -N -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-xxxx' -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' 'https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=gpt-x' > out.txt
```
We see first ~3 chunks then the TCP connection is RST/FIN and client stops. Some browsers auto-reconnect, others not.

customer_mark: Server logs show 200 then just upstream closed. No 4xx/5xx in app. Example from proxy logs: `upstream_response_time: 12.342, request_time: 12.345, upstream_status: 200, upstream_bytes: 3584, connection_closed_by_peer: upstream`

sre_jen: Poked ALB/NLB & Envoy metrics for the affected cluster. Notable: ALB's active connection spikes correlate with timeouts; target group reports `response_timeout` style closes at ~60s. ALB idle-timeout default is 60s — could be closing while we stream if there are pauses in chunk emission.

maria_prodops: Also saw a pattern where Cloudflare proxied customers had partial payloads but nginx-edge customers didn't. Cloudflare connection pooling + HTTP/2 multiplexing can coalesce and sometimes buffer before sending frames. If our runtime emits small bursts with long pauses, front proxies may buffer or drop.

alex_runtime: Two-pronged: (1) proxy idle timeouts and buffering; (2) our handler sometimes doesn't set chunked encoding headers consistently when a middleware returns early (edge-case during auth rotation). If auth rotates mid-stream and we return 401 for the next chunk — that will close the stream unexpectedly. We should check token refresh paths.

support_john: For reproduction, can we get a curl with --raw/--no-buffer and a small server-side delay between chunks to simulate heartbeat gaps? Also need request id and logs.

customer_mark: Trying this locally:
```
# server emits 3 chunks, sleep 70s, emit 1 chunk
printf 'data: chunk1

'
; sleep 1; printf 'data: chunk2

'; sleep 1; printf 'data: chunk3

'; sleep 70; printf 'data: late-chunk

'
```
When proxied through ALB -> Nginx -> app we only see first 3 chunks, ALB closes after ~60s with `504` to client side or just tears TCP without obvious 504.

ops-bot: [deploy-bot] Noted a canary config rollout 4h ago: `frontend: enable_http2` toggled true in edge-nginx group.

maria_prodops: Hmm http2 + upstream keepalive interplay. Cloudflare+HTTP/2 can hide upstream disconnects differently. For nginx, try adding `proxy_buffering off; proxy_ignore_client_abort on;` and `proxy_set_header Connection '';` Also `chunked_transfer_encoding on; gzip off;` and send `X-Accel-Buffering: no` from app.

alex_runtime: On our side we can also emit a lightweight heartbeat chunk every 20s (zero-length data comment) to keep proxies from hitting idle. Example SSE heartbeat: `:
` (a colon line). Server example: `printf "\:

"` as comment to keep alive. But that's a mitigation not root fix.

sre_jen: Envoy config we should check: `stream_idle_timeout` and `idle_timeout` settings. Default sometimes forcibly closes streams after 60s of inactivity even if connection is alive. For ALB, set IdleTimeout to >120s for streaming routes. For NLB it's TCP-level, should not close idle connections (unless idle flow logs show otherwise).

support_john: Can we get a packet-level trace (tcpdump) from an affected request? Need to see FIN/RST origin. If FIN from ALB then it's LB idle close; if from upstream then origin app is closing.

customer_mark: Attaching abbreviated tcpdump: we see ALB FIN at 60.002s after last chunk. So ALB is closing due to idle timeout. The app didn't send any data between 12s and 70s (expected), so ALB killed it.

alex_runtime: Ok that explains it for ALB paths. For Cloudflare customers we still have some partial buffering cases even when ALB isn't in path — could be HTTP/2 flow control or Cloudflare buffering heuristics. Suggest adding `Cache-Control: no-transform` and `Connection: keep-alive` and ensuring `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` present. Also set `CF-Client-Stream` headers to hint streaming (not standard but some customers reported it helps).

maria_prodops: Quick remediation plan:
- For Hosted API: bump ALB IdleTimeout to 180s for streaming target groups.
- For Dedicated: update docs to recommend front-proxy configs: nginx `proxy_buffering off; proxy_set_header Connection keep-alive; proxy_read_timeout 180s;`
- For Cloudflare proxied customers: suggest `Origin: keepalive` config and ephemeral worker that passes through chunked responses without buffering (Cloudflare Workers can be configured to stream).

support_john: Logging/action items for Support:
- Ask affected customers to try heartbeat comment (`:

`) as temporary workaround.
- If using ALB, request we escalate to infra to increase IdleTimeout for their target group or move to NLB for long-lived streams.
- Provide nginx snippet and curl repro.

alex_runtime: Adding recommended nginx snippet here:
```
proxy_buffering off;
proxy_request_buffering off;
proxy_http_version 1.1;
proxy_set_header Connection '';
proxy_set_header Proxy-Connection '';
proxy_set_header X-Accel-Buffering no;
proxy_read_timeout 180s;
```
and app should emit `X-Accel-Buffering: no` and keep `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` on responses.

customer_mark: Trying ALB timeout bump in staging now. Also testing heartbeat. Will update in ~2h after load test.

sre_jen: FYI, for the ALB change we'll need a maintenance window if it's for a shared target group. Ops already flagged potential ripple effects; I'm running a canary with one target group.

maria_prodops: Long-term, runtime should ensure token rotation doesn't return 401 mid-stream — we need to pin auth for the lifetime of a stream or gracefully signal `event: token_expired` and close with clear code so clients can handle.

support_john: Good catch. Add a follow-up ticket for product/identity to evaluate stream-safe auth behavior. For now, Support doc draft: steps to repro, nginx+envoy config checklist, curl repro, heartbeat line, ALB config guidance.

customer_mark: Thanks all, I'll post the staging results here.

support_john: Thanks — if you can include sample request ids we'll correlate logs quickly. :thumbsup:
